Render.com is such a better option these days (and I've been a huge Heroku fan since the beginning). Render has better support and pricing. In addition to great docker support and free static sites, they support distributed Elixir out of the box as well as autoscaling.

One of the biggest appeals to me is their simplified, docker-compose like approach to infrastructure as code... I still like to have it as code under version control, but things like Pulumi or Terraform are way overkill.

Render had some pretty bad outages (10+ hours) and couple shorter ones just couple months ago, so it's not perfect either. But anyways I have also found it better than Heroku for my projects, it's even easier to setup than Heroku and pricing is slightly better too (especially the free static sites).
Fly.io's pricing page seems impenetrable to me... I just checked out Render.com and it looks so easy to understand.
Can you put actual pricing on https://render.com/pricing please? / They are there, but you need to click on each individual component to get the full list.

User says Render's services worked great, but a short-notice pricing change adding $20/mo per person on top of compute (even just to hold billing info) broke their trust. A $7 instance could become $67/mo with a couple of collaborators. It hit right after they had moved services from Heroku, and they left for DigitalOcean.
Commenter asks how Render differs from DigitalOcean App Platform, saying App Platform seems to offer the same features and more for a cheaper price.
User praises free static sites, no daily restarts, easy Docker, and support for distributed Elixir ("huge for us"). Says they haven't had to touch their infrastructure for a year.

User finds Fly.io's pricing page impenetrable and Render's pricing easy to understand. Plans to try Render for a Node backend API after Cloudflare Workers kept timing out (over 10s), along with its $1/mo crons.

Newer user says Render looks very promising, not just on price. They especially like the simple, docker-compose-like infrastructure-as-code (Blueprint spec) versus overkill tools like Pulumi or Terraform, though they still want various quality-of-life improvements.

User reports Render had some bad outages (10+ hours) plus a couple of shorter ones a few months earlier, so it's not perfect. Still finds it better than Heroku: easier to set up and slightly cheaper, especially with free static sites.

Netlify customer considering a switch to Render, frustrated that Netlify makes it hard to upload a site without using its build system. Asks whether Render forces you to build static sites on its platform or allows uploads from GitHub Actions.
Team evaluating DigitalOcean App Platform says it looks like a very similar implementation to Render with similar pricing, and asks if anyone has compared the two.
